result.system_overview: The target system operates within a coastal town where a volunteer kayak patrol requires a reliable distress signaling method for kayakers who are out for 2-3 hours. The current system relies on a group text that is often ignored, indicating a need for a more effective check-in/check-out system that can function with limited cellular signal and without constant GPS tracking. The system must also ensure user privacy while providing a passive distress signal that does not require active engagement from the kayakers in case of incapacitation.

Reinforcing.Description: Increased user engagement with the distress signaling method may lead to more frequent check-ins, enhancing overall safety.
Assumptions: Users will respond positively to a simpler check-in method
Increased engagement will lead to higher safety awareness

Balancing.Description: The need for privacy may limit the effectiveness of distress signaling methods that require constant tracking.
Assumptions: Users prioritize privacy over constant monitoring
Privacy concerns will limit the adoption of certain technologies

bottlenecks.description: Limited cellular signal may hinder the effectiveness of all proposed options.

option_aware_claims.statement: Silent SMS Pings may provide a more reliable passive distress signal compared to Audio Beacon Listeners in areas with spotty cellular coverage.

assumptions: Users will prioritize ease of use in distress signaling methods
